access.edition_or_version: Ivan Morris, ed. and trans., The Pillow Book (Columbia University Press, 1967) — the scholarly anchor used here (edition verified 2026-09-24). Original classical Japanese text public domain; translation copyrighted.

tone_mechanisms_observed: evaluative labels sorting experience into lists — juxtaposed notings whose arrangement is itself the judgment
paratactic fragment juxtaposition: entries stand beside each other without connective argument; reflection emerges from the sequence, never from a thesis sentence
abrupt, unsentimental cuts between entries — the piece stops where attention stops
list-making as a sorting, evaluating stance: mild self-distance through classification
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person court observer, evaluatively present; reflection is social and reputational rather than solitary-internal — attention stays outward, to incident.
mechanics.tense_and_structure: Narrative past for episodes; timeless generic present for list entries.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Short fragments and sudden cuts; no period builds — the reflective counterpart of the brush's stroke.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Close and immediate in observation, but the classifying act evaluates from a slight remove.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Seasonal and courtly vocabulary anchoring each fragment to a specific hour or occasion; comparison through adjacency rather than simile.
mechanics.copyright_note: Original classical Japanese text public domain; Morris translation copyrighted. Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
mechanics.translation_note: Japanese parataxis and juxtaposition do not carry the analytic connectives the English reflective voice leans on; describe classical features via the named scholarly treatment (Morris; Cambridge History of Japanese Literature 2016, chs. 14-15), not from an unnamed modern rendering.
